Abhimanyu Easwaran has scored runs, led Bengal and travelled with the Indian cricket team. He has been part of several tours, waited for his opportunity and continued to knock on the door. But an India debut remains elusive.
For a batter who has consistently delivered in domestic cricket, the wait has not been easy. But Abhimanyu knows that the only response within his control is to keep working.
“Being in that situation is never easy. When you’ve been in the squad and don’t get to play in the XI, and you’ve been part of different tours, not just one tour, I think that is a bit challenging. Everybody has their own journey. You cannot change what is going to happen. I can just keep putting in the hard work, get better and hope the chance comes soon,” he told The Hindu .
For now, his responsibility is to lead Bengal’s campaign in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. After losing narrowly to Karnataka in its opener, Bengal has bounced back with consecutive wins, the latest against defending champion Jharkhand, with Abhimanyu contributing a half-century.
Having come close to winning titles across formats in recent seasons, Bengal is eager to go one step further. Abhimanyu, though, prefers to keep the focus on the process.
“Winning a tournament is just a process of doing that again and again. Winning titles is obviously the dream for every team. But we just need to play the way we have planned. Players have been given different roles. If we can follow those roles and do whatever the team demands, I think we will be in a good place,” he said.
The transition from red-ball cricket to T20 offered little preparation time. But for him, the immediate challenge is to keep Bengal winning. The India dream, meanwhile, refuses to fade.
